name: Fundació Joan Miró
funding: Private foundation; Generalitat, Barcelona council and Culture Ministry sit on its board. Strategic allies: Fundación BBVA, Fundació la Caixa, Puig. Also Fundació Banc Sabadell, Abertis, Sorigué, Damm.
watch: la Caixa's holding Criteria is the largest shareholder of gas utility Naturgy, which paid 23% of Criteria's 2025 dividends.
why_flagged: la Caixa's holding Criteria is the largest shareholder of gas utility Naturgy, which paid 23% of Criteria's 2025 dividends.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2023 and 2024 and audited accounts, naming funders and trustees inside the 2024 report.

name: Fundación PROA
watch: Tecpetrol, oil and gas, among funders.
why_flagged: Tecpetrol, oil and gas, among funders.
records_note: Names Tenaris and Ternium as its supporters and lists its executive committee and founding members; no annual report or accounts found.

name: Fundação Bienal de São Paulo
watch: Petrobras, Vale and Bloomberg among master sponsors.
why_flagged: Petrobras, Vale and Bloomberg among master sponsors.
records_note: The Fundação posts two-year reports from 2010-11 to 2024-25, financial statements for 2013 to 2025, a named partner list with no date, and its councils.

name: Fundação Fernando Leite Couto
funding: Sponsors in 2025: Moza Banco, Nedbank, Standard Bank and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. Prize partners include Óbidos council, the Portugal-Mozambique Chamber of Commerce and Camões.
watch: The Gulbenkian Foundation, endowed by oilman Calouste Gulbenkian, backed a 2025 drama workshop and is a listed sponsor.
why_flagged: Sponsors in 2025: Moza Banco, Nedbank, Standard Bank and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. Prize partners include Óbidos council, the Portugal-Mozambique Chamber of Commerce and Camões.
records_note: It posts activity reports for 2022 to 2025, accounts for 2019 and 2023 to 2025, a 2025 sponsor list and its three founders.

name: Fundação Sindika Dokolo
watch: Founders' fortune tied to Angolan state oil and diamond deals.
why_flagged: Founders' fortune tied to Angolan state oil and diamond deals.
records_note: Could not check: the foundation's own domain refuses connections and no register entry exists online, so nothing is confirmed.

name: Galeri Nasional Indonesia
funding: State gallery owned by Indonesia's Culture Ministry, a ministry created under President Prabowo; before that it sat under the education and culture ministry. Holds 1,770 artworks.
watch: On 19 December 2024 it cancelled Yos Suprapto's show ten minutes before opening after he refused to cover more paintings of Jokowi.
why_flagged: State gallery owned by Indonesia's Culture Ministry, a ministry created under President Prabowo; before that it sat under the education and culture ministry. Holds 1,770 artworks.
records_note: Its site could not be reached, so reports, accounts, funders and board were not checked; no gallery report turned up in search.

name: Galeri Petronas
funding: Part of PETRONAS, Malaysia's state oil and gas company, which has built the PETRONAS Art Collection since 1993. Nearly two million visitors since 1992.
watch: Left Suria KLCC in July 2026. A preview opened at Ombak KLCC on 21 August 2026; full opening is due by end 2027.
why_flagged: Part of PETRONAS, Malaysia's state oil and gas company, which has built the PETRONAS Art Collection since 1993. Nearly two million visitors since 1992.
records_note: No records of its own: owner PETRONAS posts annual and integrated reports for 2014 to 2025, financial reports, and names its eight directors.

name: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea
funding: Ministry of Culture state museum. The ministry paid EUR 1.5M for its 2024-25 Futurism show. Main sponsors were Autostrade per l'Italia and Enel; Ferrovie dello Stato and Unipol also sponsored.
watch: Enel made 82% of its 2025 power emission-free but runs gas plants. Autostrade per l'Italia held the Genoa bridge concession when it fell in 2018.
why_flagged: Enel made 82% of its 2025 power emission-free but runs gas plants. Autostrade per l'Italia held the Genoa bridge concession when it fell in 2018.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2015 to 2023, a transparency portal with budgets and final accounts, and its board and auditors; no standing sponsor list.

name: Gallerie d'Italia
funding: Owned and funded by Intesa Sanpaolo through its Progetto Cultura. Four museums in Milan, Naples, Turin and Vicenza drew over 750,000 visitors in 2024. No museum budget is published.
watch: About 30 Extinction Rebellion activists occupied the Turin site on 2 March 2025 over owner Intesa Sanpaolo's investments. One institution, four sites.
why_flagged: Owned and funded by Intesa Sanpaolo through its Progetto Cultura. Four museums in Milan, Naples, Turin and Vicenza drew over 750,000 visitors in 2024. No museum budget is published.
records_note: It posts nothing itself; owner Intesa Sanpaolo posts annual reports and accounts for 2007 to 2025 and names its board, with no donor list.

name: Gapar Aitiev Kyrgyz National Museum of Fine Arts
watch: In December 2019 a Culture Ministry commission confiscated works from the Feminnale; director Mira Dzhangaracheva left after death threats. Permanent display closed for repairs from late Sept 2025.
why_flagged: Underfunded national museum (about 18,000 works) paid for by Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Culture; no sponsor roster published.
records_note: A state museum; its site has no reports, accounts, donor list or board, and a search found none from the ministry.

name: Garage Museum
watch: Garage paused exhibitions in February 2022 and showed its collection again in 2024. Security services searched its offices in April 2024.
why_flagged: Non-profit project of the IRIS Foundation, founded by Roman Abramovich and Dasha Zhukova. Its endowment page lists Abramovich's gifts from 2018 to 2023; he is on UK and EU sanctions lists.
records_note: The Garage endowment fund posts reports and statutory audit results for 2019 to 2025 and a named donor list by year; two trustees are named.

name: Georgian National Museum
watch: BP, a name under active campaign, is a current and long-running funder. On 5 Oct 2026 the museum.ge homepage footer carries a BP logo linking to bpgeorgia.ge, and the site has a dedicated 'BP' corporate-partner page. The museum's 2010 volume 'Rescue Archaeology in Georgia: Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan / South Caucasian Pipelines' thanks BP and its partners and has BP Georgia staff on its editorial board. Separately, in May 2022 about 40 staff were dismissed under minister Thea Tsulukiani; they alleged retaliation for criticising the government and forming a union (ArtReview).
